title: NASA's Jupiter fact sheet: mass 1,898.13×10^24 kg and 95 satellites
summary: The sheet lists Jupiter's mass as 1,898.13 × 10^24 kg, equatorial radius at the 1-bar level 71,492 km, volumetric mean radius 69,911 km, mean density 1,326 kg/m^3, sidereal orbit 4,332.589 days, and 95 natural satellites.
body: The sheet lists Jupiter's mass as 1,898.13 × 10^24 kg, equatorial radius at the 1-bar level 71,492 km, volumetric mean radius 69,911 km, mean density 1,326 kg/m^3, sidereal orbit 4,332.589 days, and 95 natural satellites. It lists a planetary ring system as Yes. The satellite count is the count on this dated sheet, not a promise about later discoveries. Author of the sheet: Dr. David R. Williams, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Last updated on the page: 2024-10-02.
